questions.q: Which extraction method reads a database's own transaction log to capture every insert, update, and delete as a discrete, ordered event?
options: Change Data Capture (CDC)
Full extract
API pull
Flat file drop
questions.explain: CDC reads the transaction log directly, giving you the richest possible lineage — a row's full history of changes, not just its current state.

questions.q: What is the main lineage limitation of a full extract?
options: It can't tell you what changed — only what exists right now
It only works against SaaS APIs
It requires a Kafka topic
It cannot be scheduled
questions.explain: A full extract pulls every row every run. It's simple, but by itself it gives you a snapshot, not a change history.

questions.q: Why does the lesson call extraction lineage's 'point zero'?
options: Because lineage metadata not captured at extraction can never be reconstructed later
Because extraction jobs always run at midnight
Because it's the cheapest step in a pipeline
Because it's the only step governed by IT
questions.explain: Every downstream hop depends on what gets recorded at extraction — source, method, and run. Miss it here, and it's gone for good.

questions.q: A pipeline pulling data from Salesforce, where you only receive what Salesforce's API exposes, is an example of which source category?
options: SaaS and API source
OLTP database
File drop
Event stream
questions.explain: SaaS platforms like Salesforce are accessed through their API, not direct database access — so lineage is bounded by what the API chooses to expose.

questions.q: Why might a vendor's CSV file drop have weaker source-level lineage metadata than an OLTP database extract?
options: A flat file often lacks reliable timestamps or keys, forcing the extraction job to manufacture lineage metadata like a load timestamp or batch ID
CSV files are always faster to load
Flat files cannot be extracted on a schedule
OLTP databases never contain primary keys
questions.explain: An OLTP database usually has reliable timestamps and keys; a legacy CSV drop might have neither, so your own extraction job has to manufacture that lineage metadata instead.
